p.seg: De harmonica consideratione Boetius ita disseruit:
Quia neque solum in terminis speculationem proportionis habet, neque solum in differentiis, sed in utrisque communiter,

querit enim ut quemadmodum sunt ad se extremi termini, sic maioris ad medium differentia contra differentiam
medietatis ad ultimum.
Ipsarum quoque abbreviation clarified by different hand musicarum consonantiarum, quas symphonias nominant, proportiones in hac poene paene sola medietate frequenter inuenies.
Namque symphonia diatesseron quae princeps est et quodammodo uim obtinet elementi, in eiusmodi harmonicis medietatibus inuenitur, ut sunt VI ad VIII.
Sint ergo huiusmodi medietatis termini, quorum extremi sint dupli, et alii quorum extremi sint tripli, ita:

figure.note: The text implies two separate number series as individual diagrams, which were erroneously joined together into a single number series in this manuscript during the process of framing.

p.seg: Duodenarius igitur ad senarium duplus est;
et in alia dispositione XII ad IIII triplus est.
Horum si differentias colligamus et ad se inuicem comparemus, epitrita proportio, id est idem diatessaron sinphonia colligitur.
Inter VI enim et duodecim senarius est, et inter IIII et duodecim octonarius ad senarium ad senariu sesquitertiam efficit proportionem.
In eadem quoque medietate et diapente sinphonia componitur.
In duplici, uidelicet XII ad VIII, et in triplici, VI ad IIII, sesqualtera est.
Post hunc autem diapason consonantia est, ut VI ad XII.
In triplici quoque dispositione simul diapente et diapason simphonia corrected into "simphonja" by different hand componitur, ut sunt
Et quoniam triplus duas continet consonantias, diapente scilicet ac diapason, in differentiis eiusdem triplicis eundem triplum reperiemus.
Nam inter VI et VIIII corrected from "VIII" by different hand ternarius differentia est, et inter VIIII et XVIII nouenarius, qui ad ternarium triplus est.
In dupla uero dispositione, maior terminus ad medii termini contra se differentiam triplus est, et rursus minor terminus ad differentiam sui et medii termini triplus est.
Concerning the harmonic relationship, Boethius stated thus:
Because it exhibits a proportional relationship not only between the terms, nor only between their differences, but between both jointly,
it requires that just as the extreme terms are to each other, so too is the difference between the greater term and the mean as compared with the difference between the mean and the lesser term.
You will also frequently find the proportions of the musical consonances themselves, which they name symphonies, almost solely in this mean.
For the diatessaron consonance, which is the principal [consonance], and holds the force of an element in a certain way, is found in harmonic means of this type, as 6 is to 8.
Let there be terms of a harmonic mean of this type, whose extremes are duple, and others whose extremes are triple, thus:
Therefore, 12 to 6 is a duple,
and in the other disposition 12 to 4 is triple.
If we take the differences of these and compare them with each other, an epitrita proportion, the same diatessaron consonance, is formed.
For between 6 and twelve is 6, and between 4 and twelve an 8 makes a sesquitertian proportion to six.
In the same mean, moreover, a diapente consonance is composed.
In the duple [disposition], 12 to 8, and in the triple, 6 to 4, there is obviously a sesquialtera.
After this, however, there is a diapason consonance, as [for example] 6 to 12.
In the triple disposition, moreover, the consonance of both a diapente and diapason is composed at the same time, as in
And since the triple [disposition] contains two consonances, namely a diapente and a diapason, we shall discover the same triple relationship in the differences of this same triple [disposition],
for between 6 and 9 the difference is three, and between 9 and 18 nine, which is a triple in relation to three.
In the duple disposition, however, the greater term is three times the difference between itself and the middle term.
